src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_cd116_500k
cd.vint: The Census Bureau's lines of the 116th Congress's districts (its file says session 116). The Bureau published no file of the 117th Congress's districts, the Congress the 2020 election chose.
rec: Congressional Plan Modification 16 ('Plan 16'), court-ordered remedial plan (Personhuballah v. Alcorn, E.D. Va., Jan. 7, 2016)
U.S. District Court, E.D. Va., Personhuballah v. Alcorn, No. 3:13cv678, Doc. 299 (Jan. 7, 2016; copy on Justia)

Replaced the 2011 enacted plan after the court found District 3 a racial gerrymander; first used in the 2016 elections and unchanged through 2020. Census file basis: the Bureau's user note says its 116th Congress and 2018-election-year legislative districts carry no later changes. The Census 116th Congress file is this plan.

src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_sldl_500k
sldl.vint: The Census Bureau's 2020 file of legislative districts, the lines it records for the 2018 legislative session year. The Bureau published no file of the lines in use for 2020. Where a state's lines changed in between, the check below or the plan cited stops the map.
sldl.why: No map of Virginia's lower chamber districts for 2020: the election was held on the 2019 court-ordered remedial House of Delegates plan (Bethune-Hill v. Va. State Bd. of Elections, E.D. Va.; special master Bernard Grofman's Final Remedial Plan, adopted Feb. 14, 2019), and the Census Bureau published no file of those lines, so this page draws none. The official record of the plan is under The lines.
rec: 2019 court-ordered remedial House of Delegates plan (Bethune-Hill v. Va. State Bd. of Elections, E.D. Va.; special master Bernard Grofman's Final Remedial Plan, adopted Feb. 14, 2019)
U.S. District Court, E.D. Va., Bethune-Hill v. Va. State Bd. of Elections, Order of Feb. 14, 2019 (Doc. 362; copy hosted by the Brennan Center)

Redrew 25 of the 100 districts of the 2011 plan; first used Nov. 5, 2019 and again Nov. 2, 2021. No House election in 2020 (elected in odd years). Census file basis: the Bureau's user note says its 116th Congress and 2018-election-year legislative districts carry no later changes. The Census 2020 file therefore holds the 2011 lines for those 25 districts, not the 2019 plan.
